title: OidcCachedAttestor::prove hands the caller a live IdP bearer token and ignores the challenge entirely
description:
persona-attestors/src/oidc.rs:167-186. Unlike the other attestors (whose prove() is a tracked ponytail stub), this one is implemented -- and what it returns is the raw cached id_token read from disk:

    async fn prove(&self, claim: &Claim, _challenge: &[u8]) -> Result<SignedAssertion, AttestorError> {
        let pairs = scan_token_caches();
        let raw_token = pairs.into_iter().find(|(c, _)| c.spiffe_id == claim.spiffe_id) ...
        Ok(SignedAssertion { bytes: raw_token.into_bytes(), format: "application/jwt".into() })
    }

Two problems with this as the reference implementation of the trait.

(1) The challenge is discarded (note the _challenge binding). The trait contract at persona-attestors/src/lib.rs:117-129 states "challenge is a freshly-generated nonce. The attestor signs it with the key material backing the claim." Nothing here signs anything; the returned bytes are identical for every challenge. A caller written against the trait doc will assume the assertion is bound to its nonce and get no freshness or proof-of-possession property whatsoever -- the assertion is trivially replayable by anyone who has seen it once.

(2) It is credential exfiltration, not attestation. The bytes are the users live Google or Azure ID token, lifted from ~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json or ~/.azure/msal_token_cache.json (oidc.rs:104-124). That token is a bearer credential at the IdP, not merely evidence of identity: whoever receives it can present it upstream. Handing it to a peer as a "signed assertion" is categorically different from what every other attestor is specified to return, and the SignedAssertion type carries nothing that would warn a consumer of the difference.

Why this matters for a project the world files issues against: this is the only worked example of prove() in the tree, so it is what a contributor implementing a new attestor will copy. The pattern it teaches -- ignore the challenge, return whatever credential you happen to have -- is the wrong one, and it will be copied into attestors where it is equally unsafe.

Related: persona-5s4b.14 covers the missing preconditions on the trait doc; this is the concrete implementation that the missing contract has already permitted.

Fix direction: either drop this to a ChallengeFailed stub like the others until a real challenge-bound assertion is possible, or (if returning the id_token is intentional) rename the concept, make the format string say plainly that it is a bearer credential, and document that no challenge binding exists.
